profiles.name: pandas
profiles.execution: Eager DataFrame operations backed by NumPy/C extensions
profiles.parallelism: Limited by operation; Python-level code is constrained by the GIL
profiles.optimizer: No global lazy query optimizer in the classic API
profiles.pythonBoundary: Native Python API; vectorized operations avoid Python loops
profiles.bestFor: Small/medium in-memory analysis, broad ecosystem compatibility, interview fundamentals
profiles.watchFor: Object dtype, copies, Python loops, memory blowups and row-wise apply

profiles.name: Polars
profiles.execution: Rust-native vectorized DataFrame engine with eager and lazy APIs
profiles.nodeModel: Single node / streaming execution for supported plans
profiles.optimizer: Lazy query optimizer with projection/predicate pushdown
profiles.pythonBoundary: Python expressions compile into Rust engine operations
profiles.bestFor: Fast local ETL, DataFrame pipelines and larger-than-pandas analytical workloads
profiles.watchFor: Different expression model from pandas; distributed execution is not its primary model

profiles.name: DuckDB
profiles.optimizer: SQL optimizer with filter/projection pushdown and join planning
profiles.pythonBoundary: Python client submits work to native query engine
profiles.bestFor: Parquet/CSV/JSON SQL, local analytics, embedded data apps and reproducible query benchmarks
profiles.watchFor: Not a distributed compute engine; memory/storage layout still matters

profiles.name: PySpark
profiles.execution: Python driver/API over Spark's JVM execution engine
profiles.pythonBoundary: Built-in expressions stay in optimized JVM engine; Python UDFs cross a serialization boundary
profiles.bestFor: Large distributed ETL, lakehouse transforms, streaming and data-engineering platform work
profiles.watchFor: Python UDFs, tiny files, shuffles, skew, collect(), unnecessary caches and driver bottlenecks

profiles.name: Spark with Scala
profiles.pythonBoundary: No Python-JVM serialization boundary for JVM-native user code
profiles.bestFor: Spark libraries, JVM-heavy pipelines, custom typed code and minimizing Python UDF boundaries
profiles.watchFor: Built-in Spark SQL expressions often matter more than Python-vs-Scala language choice

profiles.name: Spark SQL
profiles.execution: Declarative SQL compiled to Spark physical plans
profiles.bestFor: Portable distributed transformations where the optimizer should choose execution details
profiles.watchFor: Bad joins, skew, shuffle volume, partitioning and file layout still dominate performance

benchmarkTemplates.hardware: Same 1–2 vCPU container, same object store, same region and cold/warm request policy
benchmarkTemplates.lesson: Useful for deciding whether a tiny analytical API needs a distributed engine at all.

summary: For small local data, startup and serialization overhead often matter more than distributed scale.
For Spark DataFrames and SQL, Python and Scala frequently reach the same optimized physical engine when you stay with built-in expressions.
The largest PySpark penalty appears when work falls back into row-wise Python UDFs or excessive Python/JVM serialization.
At 100 GB–multi-TB scale, partition pruning, file sizes, join strategy, shuffle volume, skew and cluster shape usually dominate language syntax.
Every benchmark should store engine version, dataset generator, file layout, hardware, cold/warm cache state and exact query.
For serverless Python, measure cold start, package/image size, memory allocation and network latency separately from the transform itself.
